Add a spatial filter to a lazy query

Source: R/intersects.R
store_intersects.Rd

Keeps the rows of a geospatial dataset whose geometry intersects y. The filter first prunes files by their extent, then pushes a candidate test on the stored bounding boxes (bbox) into the scan, and finally, in collect(), tests the candidate rows exactly with sf::st_intersects() under the session's sf::sf_use_s2() setting. When the box of y is much larger than y itself (a thin diagonal strip, a line), or y crosses the antimeridian or holds a pole, files are also pruned by their H3 cell range and the candidate test also requires the stored H3 cell (h3, and the dataset's index table for rows that cross cell edges) to touch y.

Usage

store_intersects(q, y, exact = TRUE)

Arguments

q

A query made by store_open() on a geospatial dataset.

y

The query: an sf, sfc or bbox object with a coordinate reference system (in any CRS; several geometries are combined), or H3 cells of any resolution as hex strings, bit64::integer64 or h3o H3 vectors, which stand for their cell polygons. A plain number aborts: it cannot hold an H3 cell. The geometries of an sf or sfc query must be valid, or the call aborts with the reason and advice to repair them with sf::st_make_valid() (only the query is checked). The check reads them as the exact test does: on the sphere (s2) when the query is in the data's geographic CRS and sf::sf_use_s2() is on, in the plane otherwise.

exact

TRUE runs the exact test in collect(). FALSE returns the candidate rows, a superset of the intersecting rows, with a message saying so. The candidate set is also returned, with the same message, when the geometry is not collected.

Value

The query with the filter added.

Details

The filter applies to the rows of the dataset, before the other verbs of the query. Several calls combine: a row must intersect every query.

See also

store_read(), whose intersects argument does the same.

Examples

location <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-intersects")
st <- store_connect(location, create = TRUE)
store_write(st, rcs_sim_polygons(200), "shapes/polygons",
  title = "Polygons", description = "Simulated polygons in open ocean."
)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.14.1, GDAL 3.12.1, PROJ 9.7.1; sf_use_s2() is TRUE
#> ℹ Writing "shapes/polygons": 200 rows in 1 file, and its index table in 1 file.
#> ✔ primary  C:/Users/EB2/AppData/Local/Temp/Rtmp6hCb4K/rcs-example-intersects  2/2
#>   files sent  41.1 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
area <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(
  c(xmin = -28, ymin = 7, xmax = -27, ymax = 8),
  crs = sf::st_crs(4326)
))
store_open(st, "polygons") |>
  store_intersects(area) |>
  dplyr::collect()
